place.source_title: Selfridge Field, Building Nos. 237 & 238 George Avenue

brief: Two-storey red-brick Georgian Revival house built from a standard Army Air Corps plan as noncommissioned officers' family quarters (a two-family unit, modelled here as one house) at Selfridge Field; built 1927: side-gabled with a central chimney, small gabled entrance porches on columns at each end, 6/6 windows, a picket and board fence along the street and a row of identical houses beyond.

floors: W W W W W W
W D W W D W
facade.notes: the rear of a row of brick duplexes along a service lane: each unit's back yard boxed by a wood privacy fence, back porches and steps, utility poles along the lane; identical blocks repeating down the street

why.note: Army Air Corps officers' quarters: two families per building, a standard plan repeated down the street
later residents fenced their yards: the open campus lawn subdivided by privacy fences
